name: Boundary Observation Discrimination Protocols
description: Characterizes merged pairs by zero discrimination and infinite reading costs for positive information. Finite observers and protocols obey exact cost bounds.

program.name: The Observation Boundary
program.summary: An observer sends states to records, and its boundary is the set of merged pairs: two distinct states with one record, told apart by no record-determined reading, at infinite resolution cost, repaired by one side symbol whose least alphabet is the largest fiber. The license criterion, under which a target is determined exactly when it is constant on the fibers, is proved on arbitrary sets with its lattice, its Bayes-risk and Blackwell comparison, its Beth gap, the echo law and Shannon's secrecy bound.

oneLine: Merged pairs are exactly those with zero discrimination for every record-determined reading and zero information at infinite cost for any positive target.
summary: The theory studies observers q : X -> Q, their merged pairs with equal records, finite readings with triangular discrimination, and adaptive protocols with terminal information and expected cost. It asks when a finite observer can distinguish, certify or express a target and what cost positive information requires. Merged pairs have zero discrimination for all record-determined readings and zero terminal and limit information for all record-determined protocols, while split pairs are separated by an indicator reading of discrimination two and resolved to one bit at cost one. Finite protocols obey reciprocal cost bounds in discrimination or bias, with exact erasure, secrecy and Gaussian limits under the stated nonnegativity, sum-to-one, unit-cost and bounded-bias hypotheses.
boundary: On the split side distinct records give positive triangular discrimination and one bit is recovered at unit cost, while on the merged side every record-determined reading has zero discrimination and every record-determined protocol has zero terminal and limit information. The obstruction is record-determinedness, kernel invisibility, nested supports or zero bias, which forces zero rows, zero gain and divergent price for any positive target. The results boundary_iff_blind, boundary_iff_infinite_cost and the three-descriptions equivalences locate the boundary exactly at merged pairs.

conclusions.statement: For x0 != x1, IsMergedPair q x0 x1 holds if and only if every record-determined adaptive protocol about the pair label has zero terminal MI at every horizon and bank and zero information limit.

For x0 != x1 and 0 < c <= 1, IsMergedPair q x0 x1 holds if and only if every unit-cost record-determined protocol has terminal MI < c at every horizon and bank, and if q x0 != q x1 then the indicator protocol has terminal MI >= 1 at horizon 1 and expected cost 1.
For x0 != x1, IsMergedPair q x0 x1 holds if and only if every conditional record-determined protocol has zero conditional MI at every horizon and bank and zero conditional limit.
IsMergedPair q x0 x1 holds if and only if x0 != x1 and every finite-output record-determined reading has zero discrimination, with no finiteness hypothesis on records.

For Fintype Q with DecidableEq Q and x0 != x1, q x0 = q x1 holds if and only if some license-stabilizer permutation sends x0 to x1, and holds if and only if every range-factored finite reading has zero discrimination on x0 x1.
If RecordDetermined q K and IsMergedPair q x0 x1 then readingDiscrimination K x0 x1 = 0.
Under PairMenu delta with 0 < delta, HistoryBank and c <= terminalMI, c * log 2 / delta <= expectedCost.
Given M k = 0 and L k != 0, there is no f : W -> K with L x = f (M x) for all x.
For any rows b and target L, either an inconsistency certificate exists, or a solution plus forced-target certificate exists, or a solution plus invisible changing direction exists.
For nonnegative rows summing to 1, discrimination^2/(8 log 2) <= TV^2/(2 log 2) <= jointMI and discrimination/(4 log 2) <= jointMI and jointMI <= discrimination/2 for the fair prior.

There exists a fair-prior unit-action protocol with row observations, cost at least one, zero-error decoder and finite extended cost if and only if each row gives positive mass to an output the other excludes.
For unit-sum nonnegative laws, discrimination equals 2 if and only if no output has positive mass under both laws.
For Fintype X, some bank of at most Nat.card range futureRecord - 1 words has the same kernel as full FutureEq.
No bounded adaptive procedure identifies all hidden countdown states.

openPoints: Finite-output hypotheses: Fintype Y and DecidableEq where stated, sometimes Fintype Q and DecidableEq Q.
Law hypotheses: pointwise nonnegativity, pointwise positivity, and sum-to-one where stated.
Cost hypotheses: per-reading cost at least one where stated, unit cost for indicator and repeat protocols.
Signal hypotheses: |r| <= 1 for binary pairs, 0 <= epsilon <= 1/2 for noisy and binary-menu readings, 0 < c <= 1 for positive targets.
Compact witnesses with closed acceptance sets for lifting finite goodness to global goodness; without them the threshold is finitely good but globally bad.
Classical choice used for fiber certificates, first available levels, and place families.

files.summary: The file defines certificate interfaces with permission, acceptance and soundness, and proves that accepted and certified membership imply the selected property. It defines observations, readouts and fiber acceptance, proving that a readout exists exactly when each fiber has a certificate and that properties and certificates transfer along abstractions. It develops cumulative availability with a noncomputable first available level characterizing availability and failure, and a path reachability modality with box, exogenous sensitivity, echo, persistence and a guarded safe relation that repairs persistence. Concrete Boolean, collapsing, flag, delayed and destructive-step examples separate pointwise from joint certificates and persistent from repaired behavior.
files.conclusion: The file establishes sound certificate interfaces with fiber-wise readout criteria, least available levels, box-persistence with guarded repair, and concrete separating examples.

files.summary: The file defines finite action runs, future records and experimental indistinguishability, proving it the greatest stable relation and quotienting to a minimal observer with a unique factor from any surjective sufficient monitor. It proves adaptive experiments coincide with finite words, extracts common prefixes and boundary separating steps from distinguishing words and actual executions, and shows closed records admit no new adaptive distinction. It proves no continuous map from a preconnected space can discretely repair a merged pair, instantiated by the square-versus-sign example. It analyzes a destructive three-state model where no single adaptive run identifies all initials but independent trials do, and proves at most n-1 independent equality tests suffice to realize any finite behavioral record.
files.conclusion: The least quotient by finite-experiment indistinguishability is the universal sufficient updateable observer, adaptive experiments add no power beyond words, continuous discrete repair is impossible on connected spaces, and finite independent banks of at most n-1 tests realize the full behavioral record.

files.summary: The file characterizes equality of linear observations by kernel differences and inhabited affine fibers by kernel translates, proving a linear target is forced exactly when it vanishes on the kernel and otherwise yields a TypedBoundary witness with no observation-based readout. It proves unsolvability is equivalent to existence of a left annihilator and develops finite-row certificates with soundness, forced-target and refutation equivalences culminating in a trichotomy of inconsistency, forced value or ambiguity. It instantiates three Boolean equation systems with a bottom-retaining local update, proving the bottom record cannot detect consistency. It embeds the same examples over ZMod 2 with explicit row certificates, a negation refutation, a copy kernel vector and record-preserving kernel translations.
files.conclusion: Every finite linear observation admits either a row inconsistency refutation, a row certificate forcing the target, or a kernel witness of ambiguity, with the Boolean copy, negation and cancellation systems as linear instances and bottom-only records unable to detect consistency.

files.summary: The file defines the binary entropy deficit κ_ε in bits for bias ε. It proves a lower quadratic bound from a Pinsker inequality and an upper quadratic bound, combined into a two-sided bound for |ε| ≤ 1/2. The count of readings for c bits is bounded on both sides, with end-count ratio 2 ln 2. The lower constant 2/ln 2 is shown to be best possible via a fourth-order expansion.
files.conclusion: The binary entropy deficit is two-sided quadratic with sharp lower constant 2/ln 2, giving matching two-sided reading counts whose end ratio is 2 ln 2.

files.summary: The file constructs centered binary-pair laws on four sign outcomes with correlation r and computes means, moments, disagreement rates and characteristic functions via the pair kernel of cosines. It proves exact sinc and variance-scale cosine identities giving convergence of normalized n-fold kernels to the Gaussian kernel, and lifts this to characteristic convergence of scaled convolution laws for every linear report. It proves uniform quadratic characteristic bounds yielding coordinate and box tails and tightness, and develops bounded character-polynomial approximation to lift characteristic convergence to weak convergence. The result includes degenerate correlations and gives convergence for every bounded continuous test.
files.conclusion: Normalized sums of independent centered binary pairs with any correlation in [-1,1] converge weakly to the constructed Gaussian with that covariance, including degenerate endpoints.

files.summary: The file defines finite-weight entropy and joint laws for a binary label with one or N noisy readings of reliability 1/2+ε. It proves the one-reading conditional entropy and mutual information, independence and exactness characterizations, a fourth-order expansion, and N-reading information and majority-error bounds. It then proves uniform-state conditional entropy formulas with constant and injective equality cases, maximal-entropy characterization, and fair-pair and product-projection statements over arbitrary carriers.
files.conclusion: One noisy reading holds log 2 minus binEntropy(1/2+ε), N readings hold at most that scaled by N with exponentially small majority error, and uniform-state conditional entropy is characterized at both extremes.

files.summary: The file defines factorization of a finite reading through the actual range of a record. It proves fiber-constancy is equivalent to existence of such a range factor, including empty types. It proves the record boundary has three equivalent descriptions at an explicit unequal pair: record equality, existence of a record-preserving permutation sending one state to the other, and vanishing discrimination of all range-factored finite readings. It supplies Boolean controls: the constant record merges false and true with zero discrimination, while the identity record is separated by a deterministic reading of discrimination two.
files.conclusion: Record equality, stabilizer orbit membership and universal zero discrimination coincide, witnessed by merging constant and separating identity Boolean controls.

files.summary: The file joins merged-direction blindness and split-direction indicator attainment for adaptive finite protocols about a Boolean label. It defines the one-reading indicator protocol from the Boolean indicator of the record and proves its observation law. It proves a merged pair yields zero terminal mutual information at every horizon and zero limit for every record-determined protocol, while a split pair indicator protocol is record-determined of discrimination two, gains at least one bit at horizon one at expected cost one. It packages these as equivalences: merged iff blind, and merged iff no unit-cost record-determined protocol reaches any target c in (0,1], with a joint goal declaration.
files.conclusion: A distinct pair is merged iff every record-determined protocol is blind and iff no unit-cost protocol reaches any positive target up to one bit, while a split pair is resolved by the indicator protocol at cost one.

files.summary: The file lifts infinite-cost blindness to conditional protocols with a retained initial record, proving merged pairs give zero conditional information at every horizon and limit. It builds independent-seed and indicator-seed protocols that preserve exact fair-label entropy and unit cost, yielding conditional equivalences for blindness and for infeasibility of any positive target up to one bit. It proves disjoint output supports give exclusive mass one, so the first-exclusive protocol stops after one reading with full prior entropy at cost one, and idle and Bernoulli-seeded variants attain every fraction c of the entropy at cost c. It packages exact finite-horizon and limiting seeded frontiers on the original output alphabet and for fair binary labels.
files.conclusion: Merged pairs are exactly those blind to every conditional record-determined protocol, while disjoint rows and Bernoulli seeds attain every information-cost fraction c up to the prior entropy.

files.summary: Defines readings as families of finite laws on a finite outcome type, the record-determined property, triangular discrimination at a pair, least repeat cost, and goal propositions for the record pole, boundary zero set, adaptive protocol pole, order-one residue, Godel, diagonal tower, recursion and two-point bounds. Proves record-determined readings have zero discrimination at merged pairs, that merged pairs are exactly the common zero set of such readings, and that adaptive record-determined protocols gain zero terminal and limit information. Proves quantitative order-one cost bounds, the least-cost residue interval and a two-point decoder error lower bound. Proves Godel and content orientation poles with zero repeated information, one-reading side-symbol separations, diagonal stage and limit absence with preservation, and the combined recursion clause.
files.conclusion: The merged boundary is exactly the common zero set of all record-determined readings, at which every such reading and adaptive protocol acquires zero discrimination and zero information while side information outside the record restores acquisition.

files.summary: The file defines ε-indistinguishable rows and the two M6.14 obligations for discrimination and adaptive cost. A pointwise likelihood-ratio argument gives |a-b| ≤ tanh(ε/2)(a+b) and hence a per-row discrimination bound. Summation yields the discrimination goal with quadratic ε bound, and the pair-menu cost theorem yields the expected-cost lower bound.
files.conclusion: Privacy with parameter ε limits discrimination quadratically and lower-bounds the expected cost of any adaptive protocol extracting given mutual information.

files.summary: The file defines the ciphertext law of a message under a key law and three secrecy goals. It proves that pointwise equal ciphertext laws have zero triangular discrimination. It proves the fair one-bit pad gives uniform ciphertext 1/2. It proves a decryptable perfectly secret cipher needs at least as many positive-mass keys as messages.
files.conclusion: A decryptable perfectly secret cipher needs at least as many positively weighted keys as messages, with equal rows giving zero discrimination and the fair bit pad giving uniformity.

files.summary: This file defines triangular discrimination of two finite rows and proves its basic properties: nonnegativity, vanishing exactly on equal rows, value 2 on distinct deterministic rows and 8 delta-squared for the binary symmetric kernel. It proves a single binary reading carries at most discrimination over log 2 bits, via a two-point entropy bound. It packages readings of discrimination at most delta into pair menus and conditional pair menus, proving finite-horizon and limit cost lower bounds c log 2 / delta and zero information at delta zero, summarized in boundary_singularity.
files.conclusion: Pair readings of discrimination at most delta need cost at least c log 2 / delta for c bits at every horizon and in the limit, acquire nothing when delta is zero, and discrimination vanishes exactly on merged deterministic pairs.

files.summary: Defines kinematic, place-orbit, counted-recursion, fiber-capacity and apex goals and proves each from merged-pair, place-coordinate, pole, side-symbol and fiber lemmas. Combines record poles, incompleteness and diagonal clauses, recursion, fibers, two-point bound, privacy, secrecy and apex pair into the core Boundary Theorem. Closes with the all-carrier classification and finite-label law.
files.conclusion: The core Boundary Theorem conjunction holds with each clause given its accepted proof.

files.summary: The file defines the Boolean indicator reading that puts point mass on whether a state's record equals the named record. It proves the reading is record-determined and has discrimination two exactly on split pairs. It proves merged pairs are exactly distinct states with zero discrimination for all finite-output record-determined readings, in two descriptions and with a natural-number control.
files.conclusion: Without any finiteness on records, being merged is exactly having zero discrimination for all record-determined finite readings.

files.summary: This file proves the finite divergence inequality inherited from the role-exchange module. It shows relative entropy of two finite probability laws is nonnegative when the reference law is positive. It also proves vanishing holds only at the positive reference law, using a strict termwise inequality.
files.conclusion: Finite relative entropy is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the two laws coincide.

files.summary: The file builds two validating interpretations for arithmetic checkers. A projection reading of addition and multiplication validates the base checker with induction but falsifies a true closed equation. A negation-asymmetric valuation validates the repaired equality checker with induction but falsifies a true negated equation. Each yields soundness plus a concrete unprovable true sentence.
files.conclusion: The base checker misses a true closed equation and the repaired checker misses a true negated equation, each witnessed by a validating interpretation.

files.summary: This file gives a rule-derived proof that the full contextual closure of the eight KO7 root rules terminates. It defines termination as accessibility in the reverse relation, plus immediate subterms and descent as reduct-or-subterm. It closes termination under every constructor, shows descent is well founded below terminating traces, handles the recursor by descent on its counter, and concludes every trace terminates with no weight or ordering parameter.
files.conclusion: The reverse full contextual closure of the eight KO7 root rules is well founded.

files.summary: The file proves that rows determined by content alone have zero local capacity about any finite family of counts. It derives that finite and limiting information about finitely many counted passes vanish, in unconditional and conditional forms with zero-weight initial records imposing no laws. It records the full finite-pass goal and the carrier-recursion goal as propositions and proves them. It shows a boolean test of the counter is not content-determined.
files.conclusion: Content-determined observations carry zero finite and limiting information about finitely many counted passes.

files.summary: The file states the three counted-recursion laws for arbitrary carrier type with full universe scope. It proves adaptive zero information for content-determined readings at every horizon and in the limit, with two counted states allowed to coincide. It proves one pass carries one base-two bit and n plus one passes carry log base two of n plus one with no content factor, and bundles all clauses with counter leaves zero.
files.conclusion: All content types satisfy the counted-recursion laws with zero adaptive information from content readings and exact log-base-two hidden-count information.

files.summary: The file develops finite-constraint completion with compact witnesses and closed acceptance sets, finite-agreement closure, and conservative diagonal self-extension. It proves compact closed models lift finite goodness to global goodness with finite minimal certificates for failure, and exhibits the threshold problem as finitely good but globally bad with no finite obstruction. It builds one-code, staged and directed-union extensions that preserve old tables while missing their own changed diagonals at every stage and in the limit. It derives the source-contract core goal with finite obstruction, licensed coloring, repair soundness, compact completion with budget transport and diagonal exclusion, and specializes it to readout sources with finite retained coloring and empty zero-color endpoint.
files.conclusion: From one source contract all finite, licensed, compact, cost and diagonal conclusions follow, while compact-closed hypotheses are sharp and every diagonal extension misses its own diagonal even in the limit.

files.summary: The file defines demand problems with witnesses, goodness, minimal bad obstructions, selectors, colorings, repair menus, combiners and least alphabets in extended naturals. It proves finite obstructions characterize failure and that selection coincides with obstruction coloring, finitely and with licenses, with sound repair assembly. It provides executable finite tables with replayable witness or minimal-obstruction certificates and licensed search with exhaustive replay. It proves the licensed selector criterion that least feasible and least coloring alphabets coincide with top for impossibility, illustrated by triple and denied-permission examples.
files.conclusion: For one menu and finite retained set the least feasible selector alphabet equals the least licensed coloring alphabet in extended naturals, with top for impossibility and finite values as least succeeding sizes.

files.summary: The file builds native SourceContract instances for counted-recursion, evaluated-code, stochastic-support, common-law and affine adapters, plus bounded-halting sources encoding halting at input zero and variants testing omitted premises and selector licenses. It proves each instance satisfies its native problem equation, combiner law and the source-indexed core, and it isolates exact obstructions: content blindness, paired diagonal exclusion, same-support different laws and posteriors, triangle global obstruction with minimal badness, affine negation failure, threshold finite-versus-global split, and Shannon information not preserved by incidence isomorphism. It reduces halting to source feasibility to show no computable total boundary and obstruction detector exists and no fixed-budget evaluation record classifies all successes.
files.conclusion: No computable total detector decides global source obstruction across the explicit bounded-halting family, and no fixed-budget record, even noncomputably classified, determines semantic success.

files.summary: The file defines demand isomorphisms pairing demand and witness bijections with a satisfaction equivalence, and conservative embeddings with one-way preservation. It proves isomorphisms transport witnesses, goodness, minimal bad sets, selectors, repair menus, budgets and whole licensed plans. It instantiates the framework for support, experiment, affine-equation, common-law and instrument problems, including a row-shear example where global solutions agree but singleton restrictions diverge.
files.conclusion: Demand isomorphisms preserve the whole feasibility, selector, licensed-plan and budget structure, while profile equality alone and one-way embeddings do not recover witnesses.

files.summary: Defines conflict adjacency for deterministic readings, fibers, fiber graphs and target classes, and the largest fiber. Proves two inputs conflict exactly when they share a record but differ in target, that distinct fibers never conflict, and that each fiber graph is complete multipartite and isomorphic to the multipartite graph on its target classes. Proves the whole conflict graph is the supremum of its fiber graphs. Proves the chromatic number and the least side-alphabet size for zero-error decoding equal the largest number of target values on a fiber, and for the identity target all equal the largest fiber, which is also the least place-coordinate size.
files.conclusion: On a finite input set the least side-alphabet size and the chromatic number and the least place-coordinate size all equal the largest fiber.

files.summary: The file defines representability of predicates by object codes and the diagonal predicate flipping self-application. It proves a fixed-point-free output change makes the diagonal unrepresented and the evaluator non-surjective, with Boolean negation as the concrete instance. It shows no internal self-evaluation code or complete same-carrier observer exists, while external function records read every predicate but cannot be quoted back.
files.conclusion: No object-coded total evaluator enumerates all predicates when the output admits a fixed-point-free operation, and no internal exact self-evaluation code exists under negation closure.

files.summary: The file bounds triangular discrimination by total variation above and below and computes pointwise limits to point masses. It proves merged limits give discrimination zero with divergent information cost while split limits give two. It defines the extended information price as infinite at zero discrimination for positive targets and proves finite-horizon and limit cost lower bounds, closing with discrimination two exactly for disjoint supports and zero-error decodability.
files.conclusion: Discrimination is two exactly for disjointly supported laws, which is exactly when a zero-error decoder exists, with merged limits at zero and split limits at two driving infinite extended price at the boundary.

files.summary: This file factors the dynamical distinction boundary functor as a licensed reduction morphism into a verdict carrier with equality steps. It proves the canonical five-factor composite equals the morphism and that the kernel identifies every two traces, merging void and delta void, with subsingleton quotient and singleton image. It proves the verdict map is not injective and exhibits the quotient-to-image isomorphism between one-class dynamics and one-verdict dynamics.
files.conclusion: The distinction morphism collapses all traces to a single verdict, factoring through a one-class kernel quotient isomorphic to its one-point image.

files.summary: The file defines the k-step return and the Bellman value for stopping now or stepping once with cost. It proves the value bounds every permitted stopping time, is attained, is horizon-monotone, and equals immediate payoff under step bounds or preserved payoff with nonnegative costs. A three-stage delayed-revelation example shows zero first-step gain with a strictly valuable two-step continuation.
files.conclusion: The Bellman value bounds every permitted stopping time and is attained, with a three-stage example where waiting two steps beats stopping despite no first-step gain.

files.summary: The file defines experiments with initial, target, object and answer-indexed output laws and their joint and conditional information. It proves marginalized rows are laws and product laws have zero information. It shows constant answers give product joints and pairwise structural echo on positive cells forces zero conditional target-output information.
files.conclusion: Pairwise echo on positive initial cells forces zero conditional target-output information under the answer-indexed interface.

files.summary: The file builds a fixture with a fair target and independent fair nuisance bit where answer and output return the nuisance coordinate. It computes quarter object marginals, fair outputs, and a product target-output law with zero information. The answer is nonconstant so echo fails, giving a full-support counterexample to the converse from zero information to echo.
files.conclusion: A full-support fair target plus independent nuisance bit has zero conditional information without pairwise echo.

files.summary: Defines five equality schemes for arbitrary terms, the extended axiom predicate and checker T_E, and provability in T_E. Proves every T_0 proof is a T_E proof and that every T_E axiom is true on N, hence T_E is sound on N and consistent. Develops congruence and Robinson numeral lemmas to prove every closed term is T_E provably equal to the numeral of its value. Concludes closed equations are T_E provable exactly when true on N, with the true equation S(S 0 plus 0) equals S S 0 as a repaired example.
files.conclusion: For closed terms T_E proves an equation exactly when the two sides have equal values on N.

files.summary: Defines code templates for the five equality schemes, Boolean recognizers on codes, canonical recognizers for term, formula and proof codes that check pairings at every node, the numeric checker for T_E, and the Boolean proof relation. Proves the code recognizers agree with the symbolic predicates on canonical codes and that canonical recognizers accept exactly the canonical codes. Proves each recognizer and the numeric checker primitive recursive by course-of-values steps. Proves the proof relation is primitive recursive and that existence of a code related to the code of phi holds exactly when T_E proves phi.
files.conclusion: The Boolean relation proofRelE is primitive recursive and holds for some code of a formula exactly when T_E proves that formula.

files.summary: Applies the incompleteness theorem for sound primitive recursive proof predicates to the proof relation of T_E to obtain a sentence gamma_E true on N exactly when unprovable, with neither it nor its negation provable. Packages extension, primitive recursiveness, definability, soundness, closed-equation completeness and incompleteness into a single conjunction. Defines the provability record, proves its collision with truth at gamma_E and its negation, the side-symbol criterion, representability of provability, and a second consistency collision under the formalized first theorem. Proves a corollary collecting collisions, maximal licensed singletons with no greatest licensed set, the swap stabilizer, and the one-bit fair label.
files.conclusion: The repaired checker has a true sentence that is unprovable with unprovable negation giving collisions of its provability record with truth.

files.summary: The file proves zero-error finite-cost recovery under every positive binary prior is equivalent to both strict exclusive-output supports. It computes geometric survival, normalization, entropy and exact weighted cost for first-exclusive stopping. It cuts any adaptive protocol at its first decisive output to prove a universal reciprocal lower bound with first-exclusive optimality, and shows shared outputs force a common undecided history so no finite horizon suffices.
files.conclusion: Stopping at the first exclusive output is exactly optimal: it attains the universal weighted-reciprocal minimum whenever both exclusive supports exist.

files.summary: Defines the binary erasure row with keep mass p and erasure mass 1-p and the finite-horizon repeated-reading laws and the first-definite stopping protocol that halts at the first non-erased symbol with unit cost. Shows every fixed horizon leaves a common all-erasure transcript with positive mass under both labels, so every decoder errs on some label. Shows the first-definite protocol stops with probability one, has zero decoding error, attains one bit of information, and has extended cost 1/p. Generalizes to arbitrary finite-alphabet rows via exclusive mass and first-exclusive stopping, and proves zero-error finite-cost recovery with fair prior and unit costs holds precisely when each row charges an output the other excludes, with no such protocol under nested supports.
files.conclusion: For erasure rows with 0 < p < 1 the first-definite protocol recovers the label with zero error at extended cost 1/p, and for general rows zero-error finite-cost recovery with fair prior and unit costs holds if and only if each row has positive exclusive mass.

files.summary: The file proves a fair binary label carries at most half the triangular discrimination in bits, with distinct deterministic outputs attaining one bit at discrimination two. It develops a binary Pinsker inequality via a monotone gap to give lower bounds through discrimination and total variation. It combines them into a four-part chain for one fair reading. It concludes one fair reading is informative when discrimination is positive, which holds when the two rows differ.
files.conclusion: One fair reading is informative when its two rows differ, with two-sided Pinsker bounds recorded in fair_reading_pinsker.

files.summary: The file declares exact M6.5 goals for n-ary fiber resolution and defines repeated fiber readings, likelihoods, error mass, sparse rows and per-state errors. It proves a one-reading pairwise discrimination bound, the resulting local capacity bound, maximum-likelihood attainment with Bhattacharyya exponent, sparse control with bounded discrimination but unbounded information, Fano's inequality on the stopped law, and exponential per-state and uniform resolution horizons.
files.conclusion: An n-ary fiber admits zero-error finite-cost reading exactly under mutual exclusive outputs, with one-reading capacity, attainment, Fano and exponential resolution bounds proved.

files.summary: Defines when a measure orients a relation into a strict order and the record image of a relation under an observer. Proves a measure determined by the observer falls at no fiber step, orients only outside fibers, and orients into a well-founded order with well-founded record image, with the converse via the record itself. Shows the record image is well founded holds precisely when some determined measure into a well-founded order orients the relation. Instantiates the lemma to counted passes, which stay in content fibers, and to the payload-lowering step, which stays in counter fibers, blocking determined orienting measures while the other projection orients.
files.conclusion: A determined measure orients a relation into a well-founded order if and only if the record image is well founded, so content-determined measures cannot orient counted passes and counter-determined measures cannot orient the payload step.

files.summary: Defines Fisher information for finite parametric families and pointwise twice differentiability, with C^2 implying the pointwise notion but not conversely. Proves second-order Taylor with Peano remainder and triangular-discrimination expansions with cubic big-O error under twice differentiability and little-o error under once differentiability. Exhibits the Bernoulli Fisher value 4 and a quadratic law with zero Fisher but quadratic support-boundary discrimination. Derives local quadratic bands and conditional information, cost, budget and reciprocal bounds for protocols limited by discrimination.
files.conclusion: Under positive support and pointwise differentiability, triangular discrimination is locally half the Fisher information times squared displacement with matching two-sided band and conditional information and cost bounds, while vanishing support mass breaks Fisher control as the quadratic law shows.

files.summary: Defines the forced-output emission episode on a certificate tower, with definite verdicts or refusal as records and direct whole-term certificates as the distinction. Proves licensed soundness and object-witnessedness, that a licensed definite verdict requires a direct certificate, and that channel echo states coincide with orientation-boundary states. Proves at boundary states every licensed record is refusal and every raw definite verdict has false formal legitimacy, and that every output falls into one of three forced cases.
files.conclusion: Echo states of the forced-output channel are the orientation-boundary states, where licensed output collapses to refusal.

files.summary: This file defines tables of disagreement rates, cycle inequalities, observers via shared records and vectors via unit vectors with prescribed inner products. It proves observer tables satisfy eight cycle inequalities and score at most 2, with score expressed via refused weights and a one-symbol-two-bits count. It proves observers yield vectors, vectors are equivalent to angle cycle inequalities and to PSD completions with unit diagonal, with quadratic bound, score at most 2 sqrt 2 and bits at most 1, witnessed by the extreme table and refuted by the corner table.
files.conclusion: Observer tables satisfy cycle inequalities with score at most 2, vector tables are characterized by angle cycles and PSD completions with score at most 2 sqrt 2 and at most one bit, both bounds sharp and the score-4 table admits neither.

files.summary: Builds joint laws by convolving independent standard normals along finitely many vectors, covering Dirac and singular cases. Computes projections, means, variances and covariances from the construction and shows covariance on one finite measure is positive semidefinite. Proves PSD matrices are exactly centered Gaussian covariances and that vector tables are exactly those with a common Gaussian law and with prescribed Gaussian pair marginals.
files.conclusion: Vector tables are exactly those admitting a common centered Gaussian law and prescribed Gaussian pair marginals, with covariance uniquely determining the Gaussian measure.

files.summary: Defines the checker-undecided pair of the Gödel sentence and its negation. Proves the augmented provability observer licenses standard-model truth on that pair exactly when the side map distinguishes the two sentences. Packages this criterion with the provability collision, maximal refusals without a greatest licensed set, and a provability-preserving transposition.
files.conclusion: Side-distinguishing is exactly the extra observation needed to license truth on the Gödel pair, packaged with its collision, maximal refusals and stabilizing transposition.

files.summary: Defines uniform keys on finite nonempty types with left-additive encryption and left-subtraction decryption. Proves decryption inverts encryption, ciphertext mass is uniform and message-independent, and two message laws have zero triangular discrimination. Shows positive-key count equals cardinality and the pad attains the key bound, with the two-element group as half-mass instance.
files.conclusion: Left-additive uniform group pads decrypt correctly, conceal messages perfectly with zero discrimination, and attain the Shannon positive-key bound.

files.summary: The file studies protocols that observe halting codes only through a bounded-record entry at fixed budget. It shows the shared empty entry gives zero discrimination, the fair prior carries one bit, and therefore at every budget there is a halt-loop pair with zero acquired information at every horizon and in the limit, leaving a one-bit terminal gap.
files.conclusion: At every budget there are halting and diverging codes whose bounded-record protocols acquire zero information and leave a one-bit terminal gap at every horizon and in the limit.

files.summary: The file defines occurrences as pairs of a Trace term and a Fin 2 argument place for eqW, with projections to content and place and the two canonical occurrences of eqW a a. It proves the two occurrences share content but differ in place, forming a merged pair for the content observer, while a Boolean place test separates them. It then proves the full root Step rules: the reflexive rule yields void exactly when contents are equal, and the difference rule fires unconditionally, so both reducts are available on eqW a a. It closes with a bundled statement and preserves two historical merged-pair theorems for void and unit occurrences.
files.conclusion: Every term yields a merged pair of occurrences with identical content but distinct places on which both full root equality rules fire.

files.summary: The file studies the kernel rewriting relations Step, the guarded EqGuardedStep and contextual StepCtxFull on Trace. It characterizes the reflexive and difference rules for eqW, counts nodes to isolate void as the unique one-node term, and enumerates the four contextual reducts and two normal forms of eqW void void. It develops numerals, spines, descents and frame copies to unroll the recursor, and models the observation O with its zero, successor and unrolling laws. It ends with blindness of the content observer to the zero test, separation behavior of that test, and merged step copies.
files.conclusion: The contextual reducts of eqW void void are exactly four terms with two normal forms, and the recursor observation unrolls to a spine while its content observer cannot determine the zero test.

files.summary: The file isolates the root-step recursor theory: the generic pass accompanies the root step, the positive-counter reduct is unique, and the recursor returns its content in one root step exactly at counter zero with a decidable test. It also isolates a Trace-specific deterministic counter protocol that separates distinct counters, and a demand-transport adapter where content readout and content orientation have no good solution while the counter zero test does and eventual termination holds with content blindness. It closes by restating the one-step return and a finite pigeonhole equivalence for coordinate maps.
files.conclusion: The recursor returns in one root step exactly at counter zero, yet no content-only readout or orientation is good though termination holds and the counter test is good.

files.summary: Defines joint channels and adaptive sequential composition retaining both outcomes while summing the intermediate state, plus deterministic embeddings. Proves support characterization of recoverability, composition and decomposition of restoration, associativity, and preservation of first-outcome laws and equalities. Shows conflicts and side-information budgets persist forward and are exactly preserved under recoverable continuations, with keep-then-erase strictly adding a conflict.
files.conclusion: Adaptive composition preserves restoration and target-relative side information exactly under recoverable continuations and otherwise can strictly increase conflicts as erasure shows.

files.summary: The file defines a fair binary label over two input states and its joint, record-marginal, uncertainty, read, erased and retained quantities for finite stochastic instruments. It proves the three parts sum to one bit, each lies in [0,1], and adaptive continuation cannot reduce erasure. It corrects erasure by initial ambiguity to intrinsic loss and characterizes zero intrinsic loss as pair and global recoverability.
files.conclusion: Read, retained and erased parts plus initial ambiguity partition one fair bit in [0,1], erasure is monotone under continuation, and zero intrinsic loss characterizes pair recoverability.

files.summary: This file defines deterministic instruments with read and post maps, joint output and recoverability, characterizing recovery by joint injectivity and its behavior under composition with collision persistence. It exhibits silent-keep versus silent-erase and read-and-erase showing equal records can differ on recovery and retained records can reverse reset. It defines stochastic instruments with outcome and state laws and positive-support recovery, exhibiting random reads where keeping recovers and erasing does not despite identical outcome laws.
files.conclusion: Recovery needs the full joint outcome; outcome records or laws alone do not determine recoverability or state change.

files.summary: The file defines the unobservable subspace as the intersection of kernels of all iterates, its behavioral record, finite stacked map, and quotient action and record. It proves the unobservable is the largest invariant subspace in the record kernel and equals the first finrank-many kernels. It identifies future equality with unobservable difference and gives swap and identity examples.
files.conclusion: The infinite-horizon unobservable subspace equals the first finrank-many kernels, is the largest invariant subspace in the record kernel, and its quotient is the universal minimal stable observer.

files.summary: The file rewrites Kalman behavioral equality, merged pairs and record-preserving translations as unobservable or stacked-kernel differences. It proves no merges exactly when the stacked map has full rank. It shows every projection onto the unobservable or stacked kernel resolves all merged pairs and such a projection exists, with an explicit two-point merged example.
files.conclusion: Record equality, merged pairs and record-preserving translations are exactly unobservable or stacked-kernel differences, absence of merges is full rank, and kernel projections resolve all merges.

files.summary: The file keeps the exact Goedel sentence, its negation and the provability observer with unconditional incompleteness assumptions. It proves no formula equals its negation and that the sentence pair is merged under provability. It gives the two-sided side-symbol and restriction equivalences for that pair.
files.conclusion: The Goedel sentence and its negation are distinct yet provability-equal, resolvable by a side symbol iff it distinguishes them and by restriction iff it omits one.

files.summary: The file gives the one-action linear observability lemmas used by the Kalman theory. It states behavioral equivalence as stacked-kernel membership and the kernel as the largest invariant hidden subspace. It proves full behavioral injectivity exactly when the stacked map has full rank.
files.conclusion: Behavioral equivalence is stacked-kernel membership, the kernel is the largest invariant hidden subspace, and observability is full rank.

files.summary: The file defines when an observer determines a target, what a merged pair is, and the boundary as the set of merged pairs. It proves Lemma 2.3 on determination via collisions, invariance and orbits, and Proposition 2.4 on transitive closures and apartness. It then proves the clauses of Theorem 4.1 on tests, invariant relations, side symbols, restrictions and comparison decoders, with Corollary 4.2 and Propositions 4.7 and 4.8.
files.conclusion: Every observer and merged pair satisfies the six clauses of Theorem 4.1, with empty boundary exactly for injective observers.

files.summary: The file studies when an observer can be inverted and what observing twice does, proving that a left inverse exists iff the observer is injective and characterizing inverting side maps by fibre sizes. It defines the record-choice composite, shows it is idempotent and injective exactly when the observer is, and that the non-disturbing instrument merges nothing. It proves that no infinite sequence implies no return with a successor counterexample and finite-type equivalence, then applies this to show the calculus has no infinite steps and no step is undone.
files.conclusion: No infinite-step relation has a return, the calculus terminates and no step is ever undone, and observers invert exactly when injective.

files.summary: The file fixes the joint law of N noisy reports of a uniform hidden bit and defines the error of a deterministic decoder. It proves every transcript has positive mass and a uniform positive lower bound for any decoder, so no finite decoder has zero error at positive noise. It defines the majority decoder, proves its exponential error bound and that every positive tolerance is achieved at some odd horizon, concluding exact finite recovery fails while reliable recovery succeeds.
files.conclusion: Exact finite decoding is impossible at positive noise while majority vote attains every positive error tolerance.

files.summary: This file places the chosen normal-form map in observer vocabulary under unique normal forms. It characterizes merged pairs as distinct convertible states, determination by the normal form as step-invariance, and determination of the normal form via convertibility and kernels. It shows the ambient conversion class determines the normal form exactly under unique conversion of normals, which fails on the five-point example that has a merged pair.
files.conclusion: Under unique normal forms, merged pairs, determination and collisions are exactly convertibility phenomena, with the five-point relation showing ambient convertibility need not determine the normal form.

files.summary: The file defines a polynomial observer that records the evaluations of a finite family of multivariate polynomials. It proves the zero fiber of the observer equals the zero locus of the ideal generated by the tests. It proves a target polynomial is constant on the variety exactly when a constant shift lies in the radical, including the empty variety. Failure of all such radical certificates yields two variety points with equal observer records and different target values.
files.conclusion: A polynomial target is constant on a variety exactly under a radical certificate, otherwise a merged pair witnesses non-constancy.

files.summary: The file records four statements not stated elsewhere: the readout family of a downward-closed family is nonempty iff it contains the empty set, and finite retained sets give equality and least-value characterizations of selector and coloring alphabets. It proves relabeling an annotated derivation commutes with taking its payload. It proves no function of only morphism and event trace returns the fixed-length certificate floor on a two-state system, witnessed by two transactions with same morphism and trace but floors 0 and 1.
files.conclusion: Certificate floors are not functions of morphism and trace alone, while demand alphabets and annotated payloads transport as stated.

files.summary: The file develops the Fisher remark: discrimination as the f-divergence of (u-1)^2/(u+1) with second derivative one at one, its closed form on the boundary law and failure of little-o, and the two forms of the reciprocal cost bound. It proves cost exceeds every multiple of (t-theta)^-2 at zero Fisher information and that repetition attains the inverse-square cost near parameters with positive information. It closes with the quadratic term of a twice-differentiable f-divergence as f''(1)/2 times the Fisher form.
files.conclusion: Fisher information controls local discrimination quadratically inside the support but not at the support boundary, with reciprocal cost bounds accordingly.

files.summary: The file gathers language, computability and rewriting sentences: the Beth property without inhabitance and its licensed equivalence, maximal licensed subsets of the Goedel pair, and zero discrimination with failure of uniform evaluation. It records fair-coin, uncounted-run and fork facts with recursor unrolling, bounded-record and budget reports. It proves exact outgoing transport for injective encodings with machine conjugation, and decidability of bounded halting sets.
files.conclusion: Maximal licensed subsets of the Goedel pair are the two singletons, bounded halting is decidable, and exact outgoing transport preserves paths, accessibility and confluence.

files.summary: This file collects paper-worded consequences across readings, protocols and records: fair-prior attainment and capacity and discrimination cost bounds including two-sided resolution and repetition error chains, with infimum expected cost of order inverse discrimination and zero-error reciprocal bounds. It extends the singularity to arbitrary costs and conditional initial records, gives Fisher loss as mean conditional variance for every channel via attained support including deterministic fibers, and adds kernel-pair readout impossibility, universal stable range, side-stabilizer equality, licensed-plan budget transport, depth-ratio bounds and persistent-state values.
files.conclusion: Acquiring c bits needs reciprocal cost in discrimination or bias with zero acquiring nothing, and Fisher loss equals mean conditional variance with equality exactly on common-score outputs.

files.summary: Defines exact comparisons of observation systems by state, action and record equivalences with commuting observation and transition laws. Proves they preserve finite words, adaptive experiments, executed traces, costs, separating budgets, solvability, first distinctions and minimal observers, including the surjective-projection case. Introduces the countdown with exact finite separation costs and hidden payloads whose minimal observers coincide without a raw isomorphism. Defines resolution singularity and uniform budget obstruction and proves the countdown admits no uniform bounded solver, with transport across all such isomorphisms.
files.conclusion: Every explicitly supplied observation isomorphism preserves exact solvability and singularity, and the countdown has no uniform finite-budget adaptive solver with that boundary surviving all such isomorphisms.

files.summary: Extends recursor decidability to empty content carriers and to resolving coordinates of general observers. Proves content determines observations, counters and orienting measures exactly when the content type is empty, with a joint termination and determination statement for all carriers and an empty control. Classifies when a resolving or place coordinate is determined by or invariant under the license stabilizer as exactly injectivity of the observer, with merged-pair movement and identity controls.
files.conclusion: Content determines observations and admits a content-determined orienting measure exactly in the empty-content case, and a resolving coordinate is stabilizer-invariant exactly when the observer is injective.

files.summary: This file proves foundational observer sentences: least separating sets, constancy of continuous discrete maps, kernel characterizations via transitivity and determined tests, apartness, closed test families, and unique record bijections for surjective observers. It classifies swap-invariant relations, self-test orbits and invariant tests with indicator laws and entropies, least resolving sizes and fiberwise coordinates, and unequal-fiber orbits with mutual-information maxima.
files.conclusion: Two surjective observers share a kernel exactly when a unique record bijection commutes with them, and unequal fibers yield two nonempty resolving orbits.

files.summary: This file proves finite observer realization: gluing lemmas, binary rows with a common rate from cycle conditions, and the converse that cycle inequalities imply a hidden observer, hence a full rate-table characterization. It proves a general convex-hull characterization of common laws, score preservation, separating certificates and repair bounds, with context and hidden-record forms. It records the triangle incompatibility as unrealizable with optimal repair cost 1.
files.conclusion: Rate tables are realizable exactly under cycle inequalities and otherwise a separating score certifies a quantitative repair cost, with triangle optimum 1.

files.summary: Defines maximal repairs retaining no strictly larger stable repair and greatest repairs dominating every stable repair. Proves maximal means saturated in both relation and predicate coordinates, that both endpoint repairs are maximal and incomparable on a crossing fixture, with separate deletion costs monotone in the order. Proves a greatest repair exists exactly when the raw pair already preserves the predicate, so a boundary edge forbids it while the universal system has one.
files.conclusion: Maximal repairs are exactly doubly saturated pairs with incomparable examples, while a greatest repair exists iff no repair was needed.

files.summary: This file defines the occurrence law from content weights and place conditionals and proves its content marginal and entropy chain rule H(occurrence)=H(content)+H(place|content). It defines the uniform place law, proves its normalization and log(i+1) entropy, identifies the uniform conditional term with the recursor content-leaves-log, and proves the copy entropy with a log-2 non-vacuity check.
files.conclusion: The copy occurrence law has entropy H(b)+log(i+1) nats and H(b)/log2+log2(i+1) bits.

files.summary: This file studies orientation obstruction for recursor passes on Trace x Nat with the original content map. It defines goals quantifying over well-founded relations, strict orders and all universes with an exact irreflexivity criterion. It proves irreflexive relations already obstruct content determination via the adjacent pass, with well-founded and strict-order consequences, and exhibits counter and reflexive controls showing non-vacuity and load-bearing irreflexivity.
files.conclusion: No pass-decreasing measure into an irreflexive, in particular well-founded or strict-order, relation can be determined by content, and this holds exactly for irreflexive relations.

files.summary: This module proves that record-preserving pair orbits are indexed by two records and one equality bit, and that invariant two-state functions depend only on that data. It constructs record-preserving matchings for finite sets with equal class counts and proves the full orbit equivalence without assuming finite classes. It proves point stabilizers are transitive off the fixed point with indicator-function invariants.
files.conclusion: Pair and finite-set orbits under record-preserving permutations are classified by records with equality and by per-class counts.

files.summary: This file builds the real vector spaces of quaternionic Hermitian matrices and their description by real diagonal and strictly-upper quaternion coordinates. It proves a real-linear coordinate equivalence and computes real dimensions 6 for size 2 and 28 for size 4, plus the general formula N + 4*N*(N-1)/2. It shows the 36-dimensional tensor product of two local spaces admits no linear equivalence or injective linear map into the 28-dimensional composite, while the Hermitian Kronecker products span the composite. It also records a raw Kronecker product of Hermitian matrices that is not Hermitian.
files.conclusion: The file proves the general quaternionic Hermitian dimension formula together with spanning of the size-4 Hermitian space by Hermitian Kronecker products and nonexistence of an injective linear map from the local tensor product.

files.summary: This file repeats one two-row reading and decodes by likelihood ratio. It defines likelihood, Bhattacharyya coefficient, and the decoder, proves error at most half BC to the N with discrimination and exponential forms, and cost exactly N. It proves information at least one minus binary entropy over log two, a ceiling N attaining any target below one bit, a two-sided order inverse discrimination cost, and the split versus merged deterministic ends with zero versus one coefficient.
files.conclusion: Every finite reading satisfies a two-sided resolution cost of order inverse discrimination with split pairs resolved in one reading and merged pairs yielding nothing.

files.summary: This file completes self-evaluation with an unresolved value none for Option Bool. It defines extended negation and proves none is its only fixed point, so exact self-evaluation forces none on the diagonal. It gives a two-code witness retaining definite values, proves no total Boolean readout preserves negation via a fixed-point obstruction, recovers definite records by restriction, and proves no self-evaluator exists in a cycle-closed language.
files.conclusion: No total Boolean readout preserves negation and no cycle-closed language admits an internal self-evaluator.

files.summary: This file prices persistent decaying binary evidence with actual stopped laws and costs. It proves a geometric price identity, a finite lower bound four c times four to the n with positivity, and no uniform finite budget across states. It gives a concrete one-reading protocol with positive information at unit cost, defines frozen readings experiments costs and optimal infimum, and proves matching lower and ceiling repetition upper bounds yielding two-sided four to the n growth.
files.conclusion: The optimal frozen cost grows two-sided as four to the n for every positive target below one bit.

files.summary: The file builds a decaying bias family epsilon with limit zero and the actual binary-kernel output rows answer. It defines the successor relation step from n to n plus 1, proves every state is reachable from zero and every state is exogenous hence persistent, and computes triangular discrimination as 8 times epsilon squared tending to zero. It defines the fair-target joint law with positive mutual information and combines persistence, informativeness andreachable no-floor into one family.
files.conclusion: There is a persistent, always informative binary family whose discrimination is always positive but has no positive uniform lower bound over reachable states.

files.summary: This module defines the persistent difference license as disequality of all guarded reducts with its operand interior, proving interior characterization, preservation under reduction, failure on joinable pairs, and the (void, delta void) instance. It defines the licensed seven-rule contextual relation, proves inclusion, termination, local joinability and confluence via Newman lemma with recorded non-confluence of the plain relation. It proves the witness term is unlicensed yet reaches void uniquely.
files.conclusion: The licensed repaired relation terminates and is confluent, and the witness term reaches void as its unique normal form.

files.summary: The file defines deterministic and table correlations and proves a table has a finite common observer exactly when its correlation vector lies in the convex hull of deterministic vectors. It rewrites box bounds and eight cycle inequalities as sixteen sign-pattern inequalities, constructs explicit convex weights to prove the half-space description, and deduces Fine theorem and the observer-cycle equivalence. It shows the hull has eight vertices, sixteen facets and full dimension four, and exhibits a control table satisfying the cycle inequalities but lying outside the hull.
files.conclusion: A four-test table with rates in [0,1] has a common finite observer exactly when its correlations lie in the eight-vertex full-dimensional polytope with sixteen facets.

files.summary: This module proves content-place complementarity: joint injectivity, one-step joins, total transitive closure, unique class intersections, and occurrence trichotomy. It proves existence of n-valued place coordinates exactly under finite at-most-n fibers using choice, and that full labellings biject states with record-place pairs in one free transitive orbit. It proves pair labellings biject with members equivariantly.
files.conclusion: Labellings with full class size form one free orbit under record-preserving permutations, bijecting states with record-place pairs.

files.summary: The file states the exact existence goal for PlaceCoord on the original observer and proves a coordinate forces each attained class to be finite of size n. It constructs a coordinate from finite equal-size attained classes through the bounded-coordinate theorem and finite surjectivity, yielding the goal equivalence, its nonempty-fiber form, and the empty-source and zero-value edge cases.
files.conclusion: Under finite attained classes, a place coordinate with n values exists exactly when every attained class has exactly n elements, with empty and zero cases classified.

files.summary: Defines fiber restrictions of invisible permutations and place families with per-fiber alphabets and their group action. Proves the action is free and transitive, hence one free orbit with a unique transporter, and every family resolves states with its record via a joint bijection. Relates the common alphabet Fin n to place coordinates by an equivariant equivalence and deduces coordinate freeness and transitivity. Gives a three-state control where a common alphabet yields four resolving maps in two orbits.
files.conclusion: For every observer and alphabet family the place families form one free orbit with a unique transporting invisible permutation and resolve every state, while a common alphabet splits into two orbits when fiber sizes differ.

files.summary: Defines the PR table with disagreement only at true-true and proves its algebraic score is four. Proves it admits no single joint observer and violates the final-setting cycle inequality. Defines explicit half-weight parity joint laws and proves they are nonnegative, normalized, realize the table, and give uniform one-party marginals. Restates score, no-observer, and uniform-marginals facts in the FourTestTables namespace.
files.conclusion: The PR table has score four with no joint observer and is realized by half-weight parity joints giving uniform report marginals.

files.summary: This file defines arithmetic definability with fresh variables above 53 and environment updates, with pairing and beta evaluation lemmas. It defines the precoding sequence and recursion formula and proves the formula correct via beta-coded finite sequences. It proves Godel Proposition VII that every Nat.Primrec function is definable by induction on its generation.
files.conclusion: Every primitive recursive function has an arithmetic definition at all variable pairs at least 53.

files.summary: Defines summed active mass below a horizon. Proves the drift identity expressing stopped mass of a potential with one-step mean drift d via prior mass plus d times summed active mass. Proves growth by one-horizon active mass, summation over horizons, unit-cost expected cost as summed active mass, nonnegativity, and vanishing of active mass under a uniform bound.
files.conclusion: The stopped mass satisfies the drift identity with summed active mass, unit-cost expected cost equals that sum, and a bounded sum forces active mass to zero.

files.summary: The file defines finite-horizon and limit family frontiers as infima of costs of qualifying protocols, with infinity for empty qualifying families. It proves every qualifying binary-menu family pays at least c over 4 epsilon squared in both horizons, including infinite extended cost. It lifts finite protocols to one-record conditional protocols preserving information and cost, and shows families containing majority protocols achieve the target within log of 1 over 2 eta over 2 epsilon squared plus 3 in both horizons.
files.conclusion: Binary-menu families need at least c over 4 epsilon squared to reach information c, and majority-containing families reach it within the stated logarithmic upper bound in both horizons.

files.summary: The file defines finite probability laws, entropy and mutual information in bits, and a signed-bias binary channel with its joint law and capacity envelopes. It builds finite adaptive protocols with history-dependent policy, observation, stopping, and cost, with stopped masses, terminal mutual information, and expected cost, plus conditional versions carrying initial side information. It proves per-step entropy telescopes, local capacity bounds, and finite-horizon and limiting information-cost inequalities, specialized to binary menus with quadratic and exact binary-symmetric capacities. It adds relabeling isomorphisms for protocols and tasks, a feasible-frontier framework with least costs, and concrete binary-task controls separating feasible from infeasible, probability from support, license from law, and cost from law.
files.conclusion: Every admissible adaptive binary experiment obeys an inverse-square information-cost frontier, exactly binaryCapacity in the limit, preserved under relabeling but not by equal support, license loss, or cost change alone.

files.summary: Proves an explicit positive signal radius from finite budget and information target. Shows every reading count within budget falls below the target inside that radius, including zero counts. Packages the quadratic ceiling, inverse-square minimum reading count, and bounded failure into a single resolution-cost statement.
files.conclusion: Every finite reading budget fails below any target inside an explicit positive signal radius, with quadratic ceiling and inverse-square minimum cost.

files.summary: This file proves record-choice sentences: the idempotent composite merges exactly as q does and distinct choices give distinct composites. It defines the fiberwise exchange of two choices as an invisible involution conjugating the composites. It proves conjugation closure gives one orbit, characterizes the stabilizer as fixing chosen states, and proves freeness exactly when no fiber has three states.
files.conclusion: Record choices form one invisible-group orbit with stabilizer fixing chosen states, free exactly without three-point fibers.

files.summary: The file studies an observer q : X → Q with a record choice u picking one state per record, and the idempotent state transition e = u ∘ q. It characterizes the greatest compatible relation M_e and proves a relation realizes e iff its steps stay inside one q-fiber from an unchosen state and every state reaches its chosen state, with conversion equal to the kernel of q. It proves e has a least realization iff the conjugation action fixing chosen states is free, iff no q-fiber contains three distinct states, with the least realization then sending each unchosen state directly to its chosen state. It illustrates the bound with a two-state Bool example that has a least realization and a three-state Fin 3 example that has none.
files.conclusion: Under the section hypothesis, a record-choice transition has a least realization, necessarily the direct-to-chosen relation RootStar, iff no observer fiber contains three distinct states.

files.summary: Defines the uncounted self-loop relation and its constant run, and the counted pass relation on T x Nat with content, counter and observed-test observers. Proves the self-loop returns and has an infinite run whose state determines only constant targets, so the zero-test on passes is not state-determined. Proves the counted passes have no infinite sequence or return, are well-founded, have run length exactly the starting counter, keep content constant while the counter orients, and that orienting measures and the observed test are counter-determined but not content-determined. Defines left-entropy and the zero-test on passes and proves the content leaves log (n+1) with one bit for one pass, the counter leaves zero, and the entropy split for the zero-test.
files.conclusion: The counted pass relation is well-founded and oriented by the counter, which alone determines the observed test and whose entropy cost separates content from counter.

files.summary: The file builds the majority protocol that reads a fair bit through N independent binary-symmetric readings of bias ε at unit cost and stops at N. It computes its paid cost, the likelihood structure of histories, and the error of majority decoding over 2n+1 readings. It proves a binary Fano bound by concavity of binary entropy and turns the error bound into an information lower bound. Together these give a two-sided resolution-cost bound whose exponent in ε is two on both sides.
files.conclusion: The ε⁻² resolution-cost lower bound is sharp, attained up to constants by majority voting over 2n+1 readings.

files.summary: The file defines the resolution task family, its finite-horizon, limit, and confidence minimum costs, and a reading strategy that stops at N. It embeds the majority protocol into the task by a protocol isomorphism and computes its information and cost. It proves explicit two-sided bounds for all three minima and abstracts them into inverse-square scaling plus exact capacity lower bounds. It also shows budget feasibility is preserved under demand isomorphisms.
files.conclusion: Every fixed information target below one bit has least finite-horizon, extended, and confidence-constrained cost of order ε⁻² from both sides.

files.summary: The file formalises bounded evaluation records, padding codes that hide computation budget, and the halting test. It proves Rice's theorem that a computable extensional Boolean test is constant and exhibits opposite-labelled codes sharing any bounded record. It derives zero-discrimination and zero-information poles for record-determined readings and shows halting is the union of bounded tests, semidecidable with non-semidecidable complement. Bounded records determine evaluation but are strictly finer.
files.conclusion: No nonconstant extensional Boolean test is computable, and bounded records determine but strictly refine program semantics.

files.summary: Defines the counter, ruin stopping predicate, unit and fair-coin laws, and the symmetric ruin walk protocol that moves the counter by plus or minus one with equal chance, unit cost, and stops at 0 or N, with one step law under both values of a fair label. Proves the pair is merged at every reading so terminal mutual information is zero at every horizon and zero in the limit. Defines the potential c(N-c) and proves it drops by one at every unstopped history, giving the drift identity. Deduces the summed active mass and expected cost are at most k(N-k), the walk stops with probability one, expected cost tends to k(N-k), and this bound grows without bound as barriers recede.
files.conclusion: The symmetric ruin walk acquires zero information at every horizon yet stops with probability one with expected cost exactly k(N-k) in the limit.

files.summary: The file defines discrete priors with possibly infinite support and the ciphertext marginal, law, and joint message-ciphertext law for finite ciphertexts. It proves the Shannon information identity without subtracting infinite entropies and that finite-support priors embed with matching information. It proves equal rows give zero information for every discrete prior and conversely, yielding the every-prior secrecy equivalence. A geometric prior and fair-coin example show the result beyond finite support.
files.conclusion: Equal ciphertext rows are equivalent to zero information under every discrete prior, including infinite-support priors.

files.summary: Defines finite-support priors and their support information as joint mutual information on the support subtype. Proves zero discrimination at every pair iff rows are equal, and rows are equal iff support information vanishes for every finite-support prior, with the uniform pair prior giving the converse. Transfers the finite-type case as support univ, shows protocols with equal rows acquire zero information at every horizon and in the limit, and illustrates both sides with the constant fair-coin reading and the informative parity reading on naturals.
files.conclusion: Equal rows hold exactly when support information vanishes for every finite-support prior, and any such reading gives protocols zero information at every horizon.

files.summary: The file proves the finite-message secrecy-privacy clauses: zero-ratio privacy forces zero discrimination and zero information at all horizons and in the limit, positive privacy forces a quadratic cost lower bound, and identical rows equal zero information for all priors. It computes the biased one-time pad discrimination 8δ², secret iff the key is fair, and lifts zero and positive privacy to conditional protocols with tanh and quadratic bounds. A reused-pad joint row with fair marginals decodes the label, showing marginal secrecy does not imply joint secrecy.
files.conclusion: Zero privacy gives zero information, positive privacy exacts a quadratic cost, and shared reuse breaks joint secrecy despite fair marginals.

files.summary: The file bounds binary-output readings and constructs a seeded protocol attaining the bound. It shows a two-point mass has entropy at most one bit, local gain at a retained history is at most one bit, and any protocol with unit-cost binary readings acquires at most its expected cost in bits, conditionally and unconditionally. It defines the perfect reading, fair label and a seed-dependent branch that reads once when the seed is true and stops when false, with joint seed-label law and conditional protocol. It proves the true branch carries one bit at cost one, the false branch carries zero at cost zero, and the mixture carries exactly c bits at cost c, yielding the frontier that least cost of c bits is c.
files.conclusion: For 0 <= c <= 1 some fair-label independent-seed conditional protocol with perfect unit-cost readings acquires exactly c bits at expected cost c, and no binary-output unit-cost protocol can do better, so the least cost of c bits is c.

files.summary: The file formalizes one observation contract and two obstructions sharing it: collisions block every readout family and missing readouts block the full observer, separated by the xor evaluator whose code observer has empty boundary but whose diagonal is represented by no code. It classifies negation-preserving readouts of the three-valued completion over rationals and over real probabilities in [0,1] as normalized Boolean kernels, showing no total Boolean readout preserves negation while the fair coin does and is unique under accurate definite readings. It gives an approximate self-evaluation bound delta <= epsd + epsr with an attaining example, a collision-error half bound, and a fixed-point-free shift map with no uniform displacement showing the displacement hypothesis is needed. It separates test accuracy from coverage with threshold and paired families: finite input sets are passed, geometric mean error tends to zero and bounded-block minima are classified, yet no code represents the complemented diagonal and every code errs somewhere.
files.conclusion: Every finite input set is passed by some threshold code with geometric mean error tending to zero, yet no code represents the complemented diagonal and bounded paired blocks have minimum mean error 1/(2n).

files.summary: Defines one-step and transcript log-likelihood ratios, the SPRT stopping rule and protocol, and KL divergence. Proves Wald identities at every horizon through the drift identity. Proves expected-count caps, stopping with probability one, the likelihood-ratio change of measure, and exp(-A) conditional error bounds. Proves divergence lower bounds via log concavity and specializes to binary symmetric rows as a biased ruin walk with explicit error and count bounds.
files.conclusion: The SPRT stops with probability one, errs with conditional chance at most exp(-A), and has expected count at most (A+ell)/divergence, instantiated as error exp(-4ek) and count (k+1)/(2e) for the biased walk.

files.summary: Defines provability through a Boolean proof relation, its paired indicator and its primitive-recursive preservation, and a provability formula with a specification that it holds exactly when a proof code exists. Proves from definability and the diagonal sentence of negated provability that any sound primitive-recursive proof predicate has a true sentence that it does not prove and whose negation it also does not prove.
