files.conclusion: Every sound primitive-recursive proof predicate is incomplete, with an explicit true sentence neither it nor its negation proves.

files.summary: This file defines finite stochastic channels, their support-conflict graphs, and zero-error decoders with side records. It proves a decoder exists exactly when the side record separates conflicting inputs, equivalently colorings and chromatic number bound the side alphabet, repetition leaves the conflict graph and decodability unchanged, the five-cycle needs three side symbols and two do not suffice, and N-reading mutual information grows at most quadratically so any finite budget fails sufficiently weak signals.
files.conclusion: Side-record chromatic number characterizes zero-error decodability, repetition never helps, and the five-cycle separates two from three symbols while finite budgets fail weak signals.

files.summary: Defines the miss indicator, active-history term, full until-stopping error, horizon error with an active rule, all-active horizon error, and continued-transcript active error. Proves summability and active-mass identities. Proves horizon error with any active rule exceeds full error by at most the active mass, with exact decomposition when actives are scored as errors, and that scoring actives as errors never lowers full error.
files.conclusion: Stopping at horizon n raises full decoder error by at most the active mass, with exact accounting when active histories are scored as errors.

files.summary: This file defines the terminal envelope, prior entropy and slack, terminal gap, and residual entropy for conditional protocols with retained histories, plus their information-limit versions. It proves the gap equals prior slack plus residual entropy at finite horizons and in the limit, characterizes zero slack by uniform conditional priors, and derives monotone cost bounds: gap thresholds and continuations charge reading cost via local capacity, with zero capacity preserving the envelope.
files.conclusion: Terminal gap equals prior slack plus residual entropy and any gap reduction below a threshold demands proportional reading cost, persisting in the information limit.

files.summary: This file gives an explicit log-sum form for uniform relative entropy and identifies it with the envelope-minus-entropy deficit, splitting prior slack and terminal gap into weighted divergences plus residual. It builds concrete conditional protocols such as unit-record, binary reading, zero-signal, perfect-reading, biased-prior, no-reading, and silent-reset laws with exact information, cost, and gap values. It proves telescoping deficit-drop budgets imply only finitely many paid drops above any positive floor, expresses gap drops as retained-continuation information, caps binary local gain by discrimination to price gap reduction, and bounds the optimal fair-menu cost two-sidedly with inverse scaling via repeated protocols.
files.conclusion: The optimal fair binary gap cost scales inversely with discrimination, witnessed by explicit repeat protocols, with only finitely many positively paid drops and a silent reset that erases state entropy without gaining joint information.

files.summary: Defines fiber, class and top weights with a chosen heaviest class, the threshold acceptance predicate, accepted sets, masses and error mass. Proves fiberwise decompositions and error at most (1-tau) times accepted mass with antitone accepted sets. Proves at tau=1 the accepted set equals observerAccepted with refused mass R1-obs, and one-try vulnerability equals summed top weights. Proves at the least top fraction all records are accepted with error equal to the repair frontier R1, illustrated by a fair-pair example.
files.conclusion: The threshold rule has conditional error at most 1-tau, equals the observer-measurable refusal at tau=1 and the forced-decision frontier R1 at the least top fraction.

files.summary: This file defines transcript mass at stopped histories, its total, active mass still running, and transcript, active and tail uncertainties. It proves summability, the stopped-mass split, convergence of active mass to escaping mass, and that finite-horizon information equals prior entropy minus transcript and active parts, hence the information-limit formula. Under almost-sure stopping the tail vanishes and the limit equals the mutual information of a normalized countable transcript law, with no-stop and immediately-stopping fair-bit controls showing the stopping boundary.
files.conclusion: Under almost-sure stopping the information limit equals the Shannon mutual information of the countable stopped-transcript law, and without stopping the never-stop fair-bit control separates transcript information from observed information.

files.summary: This file studies finite tuples under permutations preserving observation classes. It proves a finite partial matching extends to such a permutation, hence a tuple orbit is exactly its pointwise records plus full equality pattern, and invariant functions depend exactly on those data. It contrasts this with independent per-position relabellings, which preserve only pointwise records, showing a shared reference is necessary to preserve equality, with the empty tuple as a trivial case.
files.conclusion: Finite tuples are classified up to common invisible relabelling by pointwise records plus equality pattern, while independent relabellings see only pointwise records.

files.summary: This file gates retained-record and limiting-cost results for conditional boundary observers. It checks independent exclusive seeds with joint, survival, stopping, information and exact-cost facts, conditional indicator protocols with split information and cost, blindness characterizations, and seeded disjoint-reading frontiers with finite information but infinite extended cost. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: Seeded disjoint readings give a finite-information frontier with infinite extended cost and a blindness characterization of the boundary.

files.summary: This file pairs check with print-axioms for the mathematics-only boundary-theorem core, without rewriting or kernel imports. It covers recursor decidability and pass chains, Godel kernel cases, boundary poles and goals, boundary factorization descriptions, counted-recursion laws, kinematic and orbit clauses, fair-reading and Pinsker bounds, erasure-reading recovery, deterministic conflict graphs, record-choice orbits, Rice boundaries, and licensed demand selectors.
files.conclusion: The file records reachability and axiom footprints for the full mathematics-only boundary-theorem core and its 24-conjunct goal.

files.summary: This source reach gate audits ErasurePriorCompletion without adding definitions. It checks the zero-error finite-cost arbitrary-prior iff with full-type and axiom gates. It also checks first-exclusive survival and stopped laws with information, weighted cost with max bound, and zero-prior versus positive-prior recovery.
files.conclusion: Zero-error finite-cost erasure is characterized over arbitrary priors.

files.summary: This file pins the linear-system side-record module without proving new theorems. It checks unobservable characterizations, behavioral-record equivalences via unobservable and kernel forms, merged pairs, stabilizers, translation, emptiness via finite rank, value agreement, injective and separating projections, resolving side channels, state determination, existence of unobservable projections, and the Kalman example. It also prints axioms.
files.conclusion: Side-record indistinguishability is characterized by the unobservable subspace with resolving projections when observable.

files.summary: The file is a declaration and axiom check for the demand and annotation sentences module, running `#check` and `#print axioms` on its four theorems and definitions without proving new results. It covers nonempty Boolean families, least finite alphabets for licensed selectors, relabelling of annotated payloads and the absence of morphism trace-only certificate floors.
files.conclusion: The file records checks that licensed finite selectors have a least alphabet and that trace-only certificate floors admit no morphism.

files.summary: The file is a declaration and axiom check for the Fisher remark module, running `#check` and `#print axioms` on its discrimination, cost and repetition statements without proving new results. It covers discrimination generators and their f-divergence form, derivatives, quadratic-law closure and non-little-O behavior, Fisher cost forms, zero-cost multiples and repetition attainment with quadratic Fisher expansion.
files.conclusion: The file records checks linking discrimination generators to f-divergences with quadratic Fisher behavior and attaining repetition bounds.

files.summary: The file is a declaration and axiom check for the logic, computability and rewriting sentences module, running `#check` and `#print axioms` on its Beth, explicit-definition, Goedel, Rice, uniform-evaluation, rewriting and bounded-halting statements without proving new results. It covers Beth property and licensing, Goedel maximal licensing and Rice bounded discrimination, failure of uniform evaluation, content-versus-measure factoring, counter determination, rewriting paths, generated relations, exact embeddings and bounded halting decision.
files.conclusion: The file records checks that uniform semantic evaluation fails while bounded halting is decided, with Goedel and Rice pairs marking licensing limits.

files.conclusion: The file proves no new mathematical result; it only verifies that the listed protocol, resolution and record declarations exist and displays their axioms.

files.summary: This file provides paired checks for every public PairResolution declaration. It checks repeat protocols, likelihood multiplicativity and nonnegativity, prefix and stopped masses, costs, Bhattacharyya bounds and discrimination inequalities, and decoder error bounds. It also checks exponential error decay, two-sided resolution, and deterministic split versus merged examples. No new definitions or theorems are declared.

It covers transcript and active masses, stopped-mass splitting, conservation relative to the prior, summability, totals and limits, uncertainties, entropy bounds, mutual information and conditional information limits. It declares no new examples or theorems of its own.
files.conclusion: Recorded transcript plus active mass never exceeds the prior, with transcript uncertainty summable and bounded by entropy.
